segment_schema.compatible_with_hot: identical column set to the live transfer_index table (signature, source, destination, amount_lamports, slot, block_time, indexed_at, is_valid, transfer_type) plus the same UNIQUE(signature, source, destination) identity constraint
segment_schema.no_unnecessary_payload_duplication: no raw RPC payload or artifact body is stored in cold segments -- transfer_index rows are already compact (addresses/signature/amount/time), and any raw payload evidence lives in the existing ArtifactStore (untouched by this design)
segment_schema.indexes: idx_cold_destination_time, idx_cold_source_time, idx_cold_block_time -- matching the 3 most query-relevant HOT indexes (the 2 partial indexes and the amount-ordered composite index from HOT were judged unnecessary in COLD, since COLD is never queried for 'is_valid=1 only' bulk scans or amount-sorted top-N the way HOT sometimes is per the consumer census)

monthly_segment_validation_against_real_.conclusion: A single monthly segment is estimated at roughly 0.7-1.7 GiB under measured ingest rates -- well within a manageable single-SQLite-file size, no subsegmentation required at current volume. If sustained ingest were to grow materially (e.g. multiple x current rate), the segment_manifest schema already supports a subsegment sequence number in its segment_id naming (transfer_index_cold_YYYY_MM_NNNN.sqlite pattern is compatible with the existing segment_id=Path(dest_path).stem logic, which does not assume any particular id format) -- not activated now since current volume does not require it.

not_yet_implemented_flagged_for_p5: min/max slot (currently only min/max block_time tracked implicitly via the segment's row content, not a dedicated manifest column)
unique signature count (row_count currently conflates total rows with unique signatures; the UNIQUE constraint makes them equal in practice but a dedicated column would be more explicit)
file bytes (not recorded in the manifest table itself, though trivially obtainable via os.path.getsize at any time)
explicit reference/retention state enum (currently only closed_at IS NULL/NOT NULL distinguishes open/closed; no PERMANENT/RETIREMENT_ELIGIBLE state machine yet)
segment_manifest_fields.atomicity: manifest row is inserted via INSERT OR IGNORE at segment creation and updated via a single UPDATE statement at close_segment() time, both within the same connection's implicit transaction as the data write that precedes them -- verified by test_close_segment_marks_immutable and the RuntimeError raised in close_segment() if the UPDATE affects anything other than exactly 1 row (P4 addition, catches a manifest-row-missing bug found and fixed during P3->P4 testing)

keyset_archival_cursor.key_chosen: id (INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT) -- immutable once assigned, strictly monotonic, never reused even after deletes
keyset_archival_cursor.why_not_block_time_or_indexed_at: both are mutable/backfillable event-time fields (block_time can be indexed later than it occurred; indexed_at reflects write time but is a REAL/float, less suitable for exact keyset boundaries than an INTEGER PK) -- explicitly rejected per the human directive's own guidance
keyset_archival_cursor.high_water_binding: frozen once per run_id at run start via start_or_resume_run(); a resumed run (same run_id) NEVER re-freezes a later ceiling, tested by test_high_water_freezes_at_run_start; a genuinely new run_id gets a fresh ceiling, tested by test_new_run_id_freezes_fresh_ceiling
keyset_archival_cursor.crash_safety: checkpoint written atomically (temp file + os.replace) after EVERY batch commit -- tested by test_resume_after_partial_run_continues_not_restarts (simulates a crash after 2 of many batches, proves resume continues from row 21, not row 1, and produces zero duplicates)
keyset_archival_cursor.idempotent_rerun: re-running an already-completed run_id processes zero additional rows (test_rerun_completed_run_is_idempotent_zero_new_rows)

copy_verify_contract.sequence: SOURCE READ (mode=ro or caller-controlled) -> COLD COPY (bounded batch INSERT OR IGNORE) -> VERIFY (row count + signature digest) -> CLOSE SEGMENT (manifest UPDATE)
copy_verify_contract.no_source_deletion: verified structurally (test_no_delete_or_vacuum_in_archival_cursor_module, test_no_delete_from_hot_in_cold_store_module) and behaviorally (test_archival_never_deletes_from_source: source row count unchanged after archival)
copy_verify_contract.failed_verification_leaves_source_untouc: true by construction -- the cursor never issues a DELETE against source_conn anywhere in transfer_archival_cursor.py or transfer_cold_store.py; this is not merely 'best effort', there is no code path capable of it
